clue.text: The setter has one, being general factotum

definitions.meaning: a setter is a breed of dog, and every dog has a body: read as two words
a drudge who does all the menial jobs nobody else wants

explanation.surface: A crossword setter boasts of having a personal assistant who does everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter' looks like the crossword compiler, but it is the gun dog; 'being' just links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is British slang for a lowly worker given every tedious task, a general factotum.

clue.text: One Aussies played acted charitably (almost) about disastrous over

indicators.note: about means the first piece wraps round the second
almost tells us to drop the final letter of the phrase before it

parts.note: to act charitably is to do good, past tense did good

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word disastrous is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: disastrous means dire

explanation.surface: Someone who behaved kindly is set against a disastrous over, as at a cricket match in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: DIDGOO (DID GOOD less its last letter, from 'almost') goes 'about' ERID, which is DIRE turned 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: The didgeridoo is the long wooden drone instrument of Aboriginal Australia, so one that Australians play.

clue.text: Sticky substance surrounding roots of teeth?

definitions.meaning: an adhesive, glue or a chewy resin
the flesh in the mouth in which the teeth are set

explanation.surface: Something tacky is clinging around the base of one's teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is both an adhesive paste and the soft tissue around the teeth, two separate senses.

clue.text: Dandy stuff used in bookbinding

definitions.note: the definition is a description of a material rather than a noun synonym

parts.note: a buck is an old word for a fashionable young man, a dandy
to stuff something is to ram or cram it

explanation.surface: A foppish fabric is used to cover books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dandy stuff' reads as fine fabric, but Dandy gives BUCK and stuff, as a verb, gives RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiffened cotton or linen cloth traditionally used to cover hardback books.

clue.text: Thought of French queen dipping into drink

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: dipping into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a libation is a drink, especially one poured as an offering
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A thought about a French queen dunking herself in her drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French queen' looks like a single idea, but 'of French' gives DE and 'queen' is ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberation is careful thought or consideration before deciding.

clue.text: Educational institution in Paris that's without equal

parts.note: uni is short for university
que is French for that

explanation.surface: A Parisian school claims to be unrivalled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' looks attached to the institution, but it tells you to put 'that' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unique is the only one of its kind, so it has no equal.

clue.text: Peripatetic teacher upset about graduate in charge

indicators.note: about means the turned word wraps round the next piece
in a down clue upset means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A travelling teacher is annoyed about a graduate put in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the teacher word round, since this is a down clue; 'Peripatetic teacher' reads as one travelling tutor, but the first word alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic means wandering from place to place, just as peripatetic does.

clue.text: Argumentative Cockney in 9 with arrows

parts.note: quarrels are the square-headed bolts shot from a crossbow
9 across is a residence, a home; a Cockney drops the H, giving 'ome

explanation.surface: A Londoner at home with a quiver of arrows is spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces; a Cockney speaker famously drops the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarrelsome describes someone inclined to argue, so argumentative is a synonym.

clue.text: Welshman giving Head of English leading position

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the front position

explanation.surface: A Welshman gives the head of the English department the top job.
explanation.definitionFit: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name, so a Welshman in crossword terms.

clue.text: Residence in a very cold way, not all roofed over?

indicators.note: over means the dome sits over and round the other piece

parts.note: a roofed shape suggests a dome, the rounded roof itself

indicators.note: not all means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to act in a very cold way is to act icily

explanation.surface: A chilly home only partly covered by a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' trims the cold adverb to ICIL; the question mark admits the dome is only hinted at by 'roofed', with 'over' setting it above.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is the place where someone lives, a formal word for residence or home.

clue.text: Spectacular jumper sported in Blenheim Palace

indicators.note: sported in means the word is on show inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A jumper worn at a grand stately home, as if a sweater were on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater 'sported' at the palace; Blenheim Palace is a stately home in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The impala is an African antelope famous for its huge leaps.

clue.text: Ulterior motive in handing a deed out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has a hidden reason for handing over a legal deed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a secret purpose behind an action, an ulterior motive.

clue.text: Hackney theatre constructor, one seeking extra power?

parts.note: the Hackney Empire is a famous music-hall theatre in east London
a builder is a constructor

explanation.surface: Someone constructing a London theatre is after more influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hackney Empire is a Victorian variety theatre in east London; Hackney is a borough there.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire builder is someone who seeks to expand their power or territory, especially within an organisation.

clue.text: Arrogant about wine used in religious setting

indicators.note: used in means the first pieces are placed inside the next

parts.note: pious means devoutly religious
re means about, as in business letters
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A conceited person sounds off about wine served at a religious gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' just says PIOUS is the frame that holds RETENT; tent is an old name for a red wine from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretentious means making an exaggerated claim to importance, close to arrogant or conceited.

clue.text: Old duplicator mislaid at back of lorry during transport

indicators.note: during means the following pieces sit inside the transport word

parts.note: to cycle is a means of transport; a cycle is a bicycle
mislaid means lost

indicators.note: at back of means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A piece of old office equipment went missing from the back of a lorry in transit.
explanation.definitionFit: The cyclostyle was a nineteenth-century stencil machine for making copies, an old duplicator.

clue.text: Part of canal in ancient Troy, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means a word that sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: Ilium was the Latin name for ancient Troy

explanation.surface: A waterway in old Troy, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canal' suggests a waterway, but it is the alimentary canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final section of the small intestine, part of the alimentary canal.

clue.text: Roguish son going for girl in a serious way

indicators.note: going for means one letter is replaced by another

parts.note: roguish means rascally
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A naughty son is swapped for a girl in earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Radically means thoroughly or fundamentally, so in a serious, far-reaching way.

clue.text: Scoffed too much, having done with sound school

parts.note: something done is over, finished

indicators.note: sound means a word said aloud like the one that follows

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil who overindulged, finished with a decent school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound school' looks like praise for a good school; Eton is an elite English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeaten means having eaten too much, and to scoff is British slang for eat greedily.

clue.text: Curious old chapel beginning a new era

indicators.note: curious means strange, so the letters are arranged in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd old chapel heralds a fresh age.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochal means marking the start of a new epoch, a significant new era.

clue.text: Frown angrily, boat having left

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: Someone glowers because their boat has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' suggests departure, but 'left' is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: To scowl is to frown in an angry or bad-tempered way.

clue.text: It's awe-inspiring, situated under tree

parts.note: sub is Latin for under, as in submarine
the lime is a tree, also called a linden

explanation.surface: Something wonderful is positioned beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means of such excellence or grandeur that it inspires awe.

clue.text: Food container British leftists put outside house for horses

indicators.note: put outside means the container wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a trough is a container for animal feed
reds are left-wing radicals

explanation.surface: British socialists place a feeding trough outside a building for their horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoroughbreds are pure-bred horses, especially racehorses.

clue.text: Pay system set up for a strike-breaker

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: BACS, Bankers' Automated Clearing Services, is the UK system for paying wages straight into bank accounts

explanation.surface: A wage scheme is arranged to pay off a worker who breaks a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: BACS is the British electronic system for paying salaries; a scab is a worker who crosses a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is a derogatory word for a worker who refuses to join a strike, a strike-breaker.

clue.text: Protection for plant? It's old hat!

definitions.meaning: a glass or plastic cover placed over young plants
a close-fitting bell-shaped hat fashionable in the 1920s

explanation.surface: Gardener dismisses a plant cover as old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like the idiom for something outdated, but it is a literal hat that has gone out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is both a bell-shaped garden cover and a bell-shaped women's hat of the 1920s.

clue.text: An Athenian youth leader's element

parts.note: Timon of Athens is the misanthrope of Shakespeare's play

indicators.note: leader's means the first letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: A young Greek's leader has his own element.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a chemical element, a brittle silvery metalloid, symbol Sb.

clue.text: Gold and black component of royal regalia

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A piece of the crown jewels in gold and black.
explanation.definitionFit: The orb is the jewelled sphere carried with the sceptre among the royal regalia.

clue.text: Rock band initially attracting an old sailor

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

parts.note: an gives the single letter A
an old salt is an experienced sailor

explanation.surface: A rock band draws in a veteran seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock band' looks like a group of musicians; Rock is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic rock.

clue.text: Fit for marketing, like seaworthy vessels, say

indicators.note: say means the phrase is heard as a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: seaworthy vessels can be sailed, they are sailable

explanation.surface: Seaworthy ships are easy to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Saleable means good enough to be sold, fit for the market.
